notice: RN bank batch 151: Pharmacology case studies: antifungals for cryptococcal meningitis, antiparasitics, statin muscle injury and ACE inhibitor angioedema. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that require urgent action.

rationale.correct: Cryptococcal meningitis with high pressure is an emergency.

perOption.r1: Raised ICP causes death and blindness.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

options.text: Metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days
Albendazole for the child and the whole household

Treat the partner only if symptoms appear

questions.stem: Which hygiene teaching for pinworms should the nurse give? Select all that apply.

options.text: Wash hands after the toilet and before eating
Wash bedding and underwear in hot water
Bathe in the morning to remove eggs laid overnight
Keep the child home from school for a month

rationale.correct: Hand washing, nails, hot washing and morning baths.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

caseStudies.title: Statin muscle injury from a drug interaction

exhibits.title: Cardiology clinic
exhibits.body: A 66-year-old client with coronary artery disease takes atorvastatin 80 mg. Gemfibrozil was added 3 weeks ago for high triglycerides. The client now has aching thighs and weakness climbing stairs and dark urine.

exhibits.title: Emergency department
exhibits.body: A 54-year-old client started lisinopril 4 months ago for hypertension. This morning the client woke with a swollen lower lip and tongue and a hoarse voice. There is no rash or itching.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
